BA.rationale: Boeing is in early-stage recovery with real positive inflections — revenue +14% YoY, losses narrowing, balance sheet repaired from negative to positive equity, record $682-695B backlog, and Q1 2026 showing all three segments growing simultaneously. However, the valuation is extreme and unjustified by current fundamentals: P/E of ~80x on near-zero earnings, P/B of 30x, earnings yield of 1.3% vs 4.4% risk-free rate. BCA operating margin remains deeply negative at -6.1%, operating cash flow is negative (-$179M Q1 2026), FCF was a $1.5B outflow, and debt-to-equity is 7.8x even after the equity raise. The FY2025 'return to profitability' headline masks a ~$9.6B one-time gain from the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture — recurring operations remain loss-making. Oil at $108.64/barrel creates a material dual headwind for airline customers and input costs, with ~14% of backlog exposed to Middle Eastern carriers facing spiking fuel costs. The market has already priced in a full multi-year recovery that requires sustained production ramps (737 to 52/month, 787 to 10/month), timely FAA certifications, and margin normalization through 2027-2028 — any execution miss would be severely punished at this valuation. Morningstar's fair value of $238 (revised down from $246) sits just 4% above the current $229 price, confirming minimal margin of safety. The stock is pricing in perfection while the business delivers early-stage recovery with fragile financials.
